2. **Check the eligibility checklist** – It will list the exact academic, financial, and demographic criteria.  
3. **Gather common required documents** (these are usually asked for in AICTE scholarships):  
   - Recent mark sheets / transcript

   - Income certificate or tax return (if financial‑need is a criterion)  
   - Caste / disability certificate (if applicable)

**INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE)** – what you can expect

|---------|------------------------------------------|
| **Stipend / monthly honorarium** | A regular cash award that helps cover living expenses while you pursue your M.Sc., M.Tech, or Ph.D. (the exact amount may vary by program and year). |
| **Tuition‑fee waiver** | Full or partial exemption of tuition fees for the duration of the scholarship‑covered course. |
| **Contingency / travel allowance** | A one‑time or periodic grant for travel to conferences, workshops, or field work related to your research. |
| **Research‑material support** | Funding for laboratory consumables, software licences, books, or other items needed for your project. |
| **Medical & insurance cover** | Basic health‑insurance coverage (often included in the stipend package). |
| **Recognition & networking** | Being an INSPIRE scholar gives you access to a community of high‑performing students, mentorship from senior scientists, and invitations to national‑level seminars and workshops. |

### Why these benefits matter
- **Financial security** lets you focus on research rather than part‑time jobs.  
- **Fee waivers** reduce the overall cost of higher education, especially for students from economically weaker backgrounds.  
- **Travel & material grants** enable you to attend conferences and acquire the tools you need to produce high‑quality work.  
- **Recognition** enhances your CV, making you more attractive to future employers, Ph.D. supervisors, or funding bodies.

### How to get started
1. **Check eligibility** – You’ll need a valid **SC/ST caste certificate**, proof of residence, and an **income certificate** (if the scheme is income‑based).  
2. **Gather academic documents** – Latest mark‑sheet/transcript, admission/offer letter from the institution, and a declaration of the course you’ll pursue.  
3. **Visit the official portal** – Most of these scholarships are administered through the **National Scholarship Portal (NSP)** or the respective state scholarship website.  
4. **Create an account & fill the online form** – Enter personal, family, and academic details exactly as they appear on your certificates.  
5. **Upload scanned copies** – Caste certificate, income certificate, ID proof, photograph, and the documents listed in step 2.  
6. **Submit and note the application number** – Keep a copy of the confirmation email/SMS for future reference.  
7. **Follow up** – After submission, the authorities may request additional verification (e.g., a field visit). Respond promptly to avoid delays.

### Documents you’ll typically need
- SC/ST caste certificate (original & scanned)
- Income certificate / BPL card (if applicable)
- Aadhaar card / voter ID
- Recent passport‑size photograph (digital)
- Latest academic transcript & provisional/offer letter from the college/university
- Bank account details (for scholarship disbursement)

### Tips
- **Apply early** – Some scholarships have limited seats and are awarded on a first‑come, first‑served basis.  
- **Apply to multiple schemes** – You can be a beneficiary of more than one scholarship if the guidelines allow.  
- **Keep copies** of every document you upload; you may need them for future verification.  
- **Verify the official website** (e.g., https://scholarships.gov.in or your state’s education department portal) for the most up‑to‑date forms and any changes in deadlines.

| Scholarship | Who can apply | What it covers | Deadline | Approx. amount |

### Why these match your interest
- **Target group:** All three are explicitly for **female students**.
- **Field of study:** They focus on **technical education** (engineering, IT, architecture, pharmacy, etc.).
- **Government‑backed:** Administered by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), so they are widely recognized and accepted by most colleges.

### Quick checklist to start your application
1. **Confirm eligibility** – you must be a girl student enrolled (or having secured admission) in an AICTE‑approved technical program.  
2. **Gather documents**  
   - Recent passport‑size photograph  
   - Identity proof (Aadhaar / PAN)  
   - Admission/Enrollment letter from the institute  
   - Academic transcripts of the previous qualification  
   - Income certificate (if the scheme has a family‑income ceiling)  
   - Caste/Category certificate (if you belong to a reserved category)  
3. **Visit the AICTE scholarship portal** – [scholarships.aicte.org](https://scholarships.aicte.org) (or the specific link provided by your college).  
4. **Create a user account** and fill in the online application form.  
5. **Upload the scanned documents** exactly as requested (PDF, max 2 MB each).  
6. **Submit before the deadline** (for the main Pragati Scholarship, 10 Sept 2026).  
7. **Note the application reference number** – you’ll need it for any follow‑up or verification.

### Tips
- Apply as early as possible; many seats get filled quickly.  
- Keep digital copies of all certificates; you may need to re‑upload for later years.  
- If your college has a scholarship cell, ask them to review your application before you submit – they can spot missing documents.  
- Even if you miss the deadline for one scheme, the other Pragati scholarships often have rolling or yearly windows, so you can try again next year.

Feel free to ask if you need help locating the portal link, preparing any specific document, or understanding any part of the application process!

**National Merit‑cum‑Means Scholarship (NMMS) – Class 9**

**What it is**  
The National Merit‑cum‑Means Scholarship (NMMS) is a central‑government scheme launched by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (now the Ministry of Education). Its aim is to encourage meritorious students who belong to economically weaker sections (EWS) to continue their studies beyond the primary stage.  

**Who can apply (Class 9)**  

| Criterion | Typical requirement |
|-----------|----------------------|
| **Class** | Currently studying in Class 8 (or have just passed it) and will be admitted to Class 9 in the academic year for which the scholarship is offered. |
| **Academic performance** | Minimum 75 % aggregate marks (or the equivalent as prescribed by the state) in the last qualifying examination (Class 8). |
| **Economic status** | Family annual income **≤ ₹1.8 lakhs** (the exact ceiling may vary slightly by state). |
| **Residence** | Indian citizen, residing in any state/UT of India. |
| **Other** | No pending dues or disciplinary actions in the school; must be enrolled in a recognized school (government, government‑aided or recognized private). |

**Benefits**  

| Component | Amount |
|-----------|--------|
| **Scholarship** | ₹1,000 per month (₹12,000 per academic year). |
| **Maintenance allowance** (if applicable in some states) | Up to ₹400 per month for books, transport, etc. |
| **One‑time assistance** (occasionally) | Up to ₹5,000 for a specific need (e.g., admission fees). |

The total cash assistance is therefore **₹12,000 per year** (plus any state‑specific allowances).

**How the selection works**  

1. **Merit list** – Schools submit the names of eligible students with their marks and income details.  
2. **Means verification** – The income certificate (Form‑16, BPL/Income certificate, or any other proof accepted by the state) is verified by the school/education department.  
3. **Final list** – A merit‑cum‑means list is prepared and the scholarship is awarded to those who satisfy both criteria.

**Application / enrollment process**  

1. **Check with your school** – Most schools handle the entire process: they collect documents, fill out the application form, and forward it to the district education office.  
2. **Documents usually required**  
   * Class 8 mark sheet (original & photocopy)  
   * Income certificate of the family (≤ ₹1.8 lakhs) – can be a BPL certificate, income certificate from the Tahsildar, or an affidavit with salary slips.  
   * Caste certificate (if you belong to a reserved category – not mandatory for the scholarship but may be needed for other schemes).  
   * Birth certificate / school admission proof.  
   * Recent passport‑size photograph.  
3. **Form** – The school provides the **NMMS application form** (often called “Form‑1” or “NMMS Application”). Fill it accurately.  
4. **Submission deadline** – The central deadline varies each year (usually around **April–May** for the upcoming academic session). Since the exact date isn’t listed in the data you have, ask your school or check the official portal for the current year’s cut‑off.  
5. **Verification** – After submission, the district officials verify the income and academic documents.  
6. **Award letter** – If selected, you’ll receive a scholarship award letter. The scholarship amount is usually credited directly to the student’s bank account (or via a cheque to the school, which then disburses it).  

**Things to keep in mind**

* **Multiple applications** – If you qualify for other state or private scholarships, you can apply for them simultaneously; NMMS does not restrict you from receiving additional aid.  
* **Renewal** – To continue receiving the scholarship in Class 10 and beyond, you must maintain the academic (≥ 75 %) and income criteria each year and re‑apply through your school.  
* **Stay updated** – The Ministry of Education’s portal (https://scholarships.gov.in) publishes the latest guidelines, forms, and deadlines each year.  

**Quick checklist for a Class 9 student**

- [ ] 75 %+ marks in Class 8 board exams  
- [ ] Family annual income ≤ ₹1.8 lakhs (obtain income certificate)  
- [ ] Collect school mark sheet, birth certificate, passport‑size photos  
- [ ] Talk to your school’s counselor or principal about the NMMS form and the submission deadline for this academic year  
- [ ] Submit the form with all documents on time  

If you need help locating the official form or have any specific doubts about the documents, let me know—I’m happy to guide you through the next steps!

It is named after the folk‑hero **Devnarayan** and is part of Rajasthan’s effort to improve the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) among disadvantaged groups. | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Target group** | • SC, OBC, and other eligible backward‑class students
• Residents of Rajasthan (usually those who have studied in a government or recognized private school in the state) | | **Education levels covered** | • Post‑Matriculation (class 11‑12)
• Undergraduate (undergrad + professional courses)
• Post‑graduate and diploma courses | | **Purpose** | • Provide financial assistance to cover tuition fees, books, lab fees, residence, and other education‑related expenses
• Reduce dropout rates among socially‑backward students | | **Amount** | Varies by course and family income. Typical disbursements range from **₹ 10,000 – ₹ 50,000** per year, paid in installments. The exact figure is decided by the state’s Backward Classes Welfare Department. | | **Eligibility criteria (general)** | 1. **Caste certificate** of SC/OBC (or any other category specified by the scheme).
2. **Annual family income** not exceeding the ceiling set for the scheme (often around **₹ 2,50,000** for the poorest households).
3. **Academic performance** – a minimum of **45 %** (or 5‑point CGPA) in the previous qualifying exam.

4. **Fill in the online form** – upload scanned copies of required documents (photo, ID, caste/income certificates, mark sheets, admission letter).  
5. **Submit before the deadline** – note the dates above; late submissions are usually not accepted.  
6. **Track your application** – the portal lets you see the status and any additional documents requested.

- Apply to **all** scholarships you meet the criteria for; there’s no penalty for multiple applications.
